SUBJECT:  APPROVE FIRST AMENDMENT WITH WILSON EVENTS

  YEAR TERM

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the City Council:

  1. Approve First Amendment Agreement No. A-8504 with Wilson Events
  Incorporated for booking and onsite production services, increasing the
  agreement by $335,680 for a total not to exceed amount of $585,680 for a term of
  one year with an option to extend an additional one-year term;

  2. Authorize the Interim City Manager or his designee to execute First Amendment
  Agreement No. A-8504 with Wilson Events Incorporated, including minimal
  and/or non-substantial changes; and,

  3. Authorize the Interim City Manager or his designee to exercise the option to
  extend one additional one-year term.

BACKGROUND

Professional entertainment booking and management services are standard practice in
the industry. To secure nationally recognized artists and manage complex contracts, the
City contracts with Wilson Events, Inc., for headline entertainment booking services.
These professional services include entertainers, performers, and specialty services for
parks and recreation programs.

The Agreement is non-exclusive. The City may also secure entertainers directly or
through other talent buyers as needed. The Agreement was executed pursuant to
Ordinance No. 1599, Section 3.08.140, which exempts certain professional services from
the competitive bidding process and requires selection based on qualifications.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Approve First Amendment to Agreement No. A-8504 Wilson Events Incorporated
February 18, 2026
Page 2

DISCUSSION

This action authorizes additional funding to continue services and exercise an additional
year of the existing agreement, with no changes to the scope of services or fee structure.
Approval of the First Amendment will increase the contract amount by $335,680 to fund
artist booking services for the upcoming contract year and any remaining option years.

Wilson Events’ established industry reputation enables the City to secure a diverse range
of high-quality, nationally recognized artists. The firm’s experience representing the
venue ensures compliance with City requirements and artist standards, supporting the
delivery of well-managed, high-quality, and safe performances for the community.

Under the agreement, Wilson Events provides turnkey booking services, including artist
procurement, contract negotiation, production coordination, and on-site artist
management. As a major talent buyer in the Western United States, the firm leverages
its industry relationships and client base to secure competitive pricing and access to
touring artists. Wilson Events maintains ongoing communication with national artist
agencies and talent management companies to monitor availability and touring
schedules. Over the past 30 years, the firm has purchased nearly $500 million in talent
and served clients nationwide.

FISCAL IMPACT

$335,680; Sufficient funds for these services are budgeted in Parks and Recreation
Concert Program account. Annual funding necessary will be evaluated and approved
as part of the City’s budget adoption process.

STRATEGIC PLAN

Goal IV: Maintain a desirable community where everyone wants to live, work, and
play.

  D. Develop and maintain diverse programs and events that inspire growth, pride,
  and lifelong learning.

1  CITY PROJECT MANAGER

• Consult and develop a talent plan including projections of budget and program

Concert Series.

• Secure booking for Palmdale Concert Series and facilitate City contact and
insurance requirements.

• Identify, review and facilitate all backline and rider requirements.

• The Proposer should be qualified in the following:

  • Demonstrated ability to secure timely booking of quality regional and national
  acts.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the City Council:

  1. Authorize an Energy Storage Resource Adequacy Agreement between Circle City
  Energy Storage LLC, an ENGIE company, and California Choice Energy Authority
  (CalChoice), on behalf of EPIC, for the purchase of Resource Adequacy (RA) and
  long-term, mid-term reliability capacity for a term of ten years; and,

  2. Authorize the Interim City Manager, or his designee, to execute a Resource
  Adequacy Agreement, subject to the approval of the City Attorney.

BACKGROUND

The City’s Community Choice Aggregation (CCA) Program, Energy for Palmdale’s
Independent Choice (EPIC), was established by the City Council through adoption of
Resolution No. CC 2018-087 on December 4, 2018. The Program successfully began
serving customers on October 1, 2022. The actions before the City Council are in support
of this effort.

To ensure long-term grid reliability for its customers and meet state-mandated
procurement requirements, EPIC, through CalChoice, participates in the procurement of
Resource Adequacy (RA) Capacity.

DISCUSSION

The California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) previously issued Decision (D.) 21-06-
035, and subsequently Decision (D.) 23-02-040, the latter of which mandates that load-
serving entities, including CCAs, collectively procure substantial incremental capacity
over a phased schedule reflecting two distinct compliance deadlines: June 1, 2026, and
June 1, 2027. This procurement is intended to bolster system reliability by adding to
California’s resource fleet.

To further support meeting the CPUC’s mid-term reliability procurement mandate,
CalChoice’s technical team identified a procurement opportunity associated with a
standalone four-hour Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) located in the City of
Corona, Riverside County. The project, Circle City Energy Storage, is being developed
by ENGIE and has a total nameplate or maximum rated output capacity of 85 megawatts
(MW), which can be dispatched over a four-hour period, providing up to 340 megawatt
hours (MWh) to the grid.

The amount of capacity that has yet to be contracted from this facility is 17 MW, which is
expected to achieve commercial operation on June 1, 2026. Note that this portion of the
project will be constructed and contracted as a separately metered phase. CalChoice
plans to contract, amongst various members, for the entirety of this capacity balance by
arranging separate 10-year Energy Storage Resource Adequacy Agreements for each
participating member.

EPIC’s “Member’s Share” of this allocation will be approximately 19%, equating to 3.25
MW of the project’s capacity. The recommended Energy Storage Resource Adequacy
Agreement, attached for Council consideration, contains terms, including financial
security, performance standards, and remedy provisions, that are substantially similar to
those used in other similar CalChoice agreements that adhere to industry best practices.
The agreement incorporates a Contingent Firm delivery structure and robust financial
security requirements, which protect EPIC from project delays and/or non-performance.

As a condition of the contract, the payment terms ensure that the City’s general fund is
protected through the Member Lockbox Arrangement. Circle City Energy Storage LLC
recognizes and accepts the security provided in the name of the City as credit and
collateral.

Based on the foregoing, staff recommends that the City Council approve entering into the
Energy Storage Resource Adequacy Agreement with Circle City Energy Storage LLC on
behalf of EPIC and authorize the Interim City Manager to execute this Agreement.

  ARTICLE 10
  FORCE MAJEURE

  10.1  Definition.

  (a)  “Force Majeure Event” means any act or event or circumstance
occurring after the Effective Date that delays or prevents a Party from timely performing all or a
portion of its obligations under this Agreement or from complying with all or a portion of the
conditions under this Agreement if such act or event, despite the exercise of reasonable efforts,
cannot be avoided by and is beyond the reasonable control (whether direct or indirect) of and
without the fault or negligence of the Party relying thereon as justification for such delay,
nonperformance, or noncompliance.

  (b)  Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, so long as the following
events, despite the exercise of reasonable efforts, cannot be avoided by, and are beyond the
reasonable control (whether direct or indirect) of and without the fault or negligence of the Party
relying thereon as justification for such delay, nonperformance or noncompliance, a Force
Majeure Event shall include: an act of God or the elements, such as flooding, lightning,
hurricanes, tornadoes, or ice storms; explosion; fire; volcanic eruption; flood; epidemic;

  31
 pandemic, landslide; mudslide; sabotage; terrorism; earthquake; or other cataclysmic events; an
act of public enemy; war; blockade; civil insurrection; riot; civil disturbance; strikes or other
labor difficulties caused or suffered by a Party or any third party; delays resulting from action or
inaction of a local public permitting authority; and any temporary restraint or restriction imposed
by applicable Law or any directive from a Governmental Authority.

  (c)  Notwithstanding the foregoing, the term “Force Majeure Event” does not
include (i) economic conditions that render a Party’s performance of this Agreement at the
Contract Price unprofitable or otherwise uneconomic (including Buyer’s ability to buy the
Product at a lower price, or Seller’s ability to sell Product at a higher price, than the Contract
Price); (ii) Seller’s inability to obtain permits or approvals of any type for the construction,
operation, or maintenance of the Facility except to the extent such inability is caused by a Force
Majeure Event; (iii) the inability of a Party to make payments when due under this Agreement,
unless the cause of such inability is an event that would otherwise constitute a Force Majeure
Event as described above that disables physical or electronic facilities necessary to transfer funds
to the payee Party; (iv) Seller’s inability to obtain sufficient labor, equipment, materials, or other
resources to build or operate the Facility except to the extent such inability is caused by a Force
Majeure Event; (v) a strike, work stoppage or labor dispute limited only to any one or more of
Seller, Seller’s Affiliates, Seller’s contractors, their subcontractors thereof or any other third
party employed by Seller to work on the Facility, except to the extent such strikes or labor
disturbances at the Facility Site or contractor's or any subcontractor's facilities are directly related
to strikes or labor disturbances that are (x) on a regional or national level and are (y)
simultaneously disrupting other business operations in the applicable regional or national area,
but only to the extent there are other like business operations in the applicable regional or
national area; or (vi) any equipment failure except if such equipment failure is due to a serial
defect or is caused by a Force Majeure Event. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the occurrence and
continuation of a Force Majeure Event shall not (a) suspend or excuse the obligation of Seller to
achieve the Guaranteed Construction Start Date or the Guaranteed Commercial Operation Date
beyond the extensions provided in Exhibit B, or (b) limit Buyer’s right to declare an Event of
Default pursuant to Section 11.1(b)(i) and receive a Damage Payment upon exercise of Buyer’s
default right pursuant to Sections 11.2 and 11.3.

  10.2 No Liability If a Force Majeure Event Occurs. Neither Seller nor Buyer shall
be liable to the other Party in the event it is prevented or delayed from performing its obligations
hereunder in whole or in part due to a Force Majeure Event. The Party rendered unable to fulfill
any obligation by reason of a Force Majeure Event shall take reasonable actions necessary to
remove such inability with due speed and diligence. Nothing herein shall be construed as
permitting that Party to continue to fail to perform after said cause has been removed. The
obligation to use due speed and diligence shall not be interpreted to require resolution of labor
disputes by acceding to demands of the opposition when such course is inadvisable in the
discretion of the Party having such difficulty. Neither Party shall be considered in breach or
default of this Agreement if and to the extent that any failure or delay in the Party’s performance
of one or more of its obligations hereunder is caused by a Force Majeure Event. The occurrence
and continuation of a Force Majeure Event shall not suspend or excuse the obligation of a Party
to make any payments due hereunder.

   10.3 Notice. Within ten (10) Business Days of becoming aware of the commencement

  STORAGE CAPACITY TESTS

Storage Capacity Test Notice and Frequency

  A.  Storage Capacity Test. Upon no less than ten (10) Business Days prior Notice to
Buyer, Seller shall schedule and complete a Storage Capacity Test prior to the Commercial
Operation Date. Such initial Storage Capacity Test and any subsequent Commercial Operation
Storage Capacity Test conducted pursuant to Section 4.7 shall be performed in accordance with
this Exhibit L and shall establish the Effective Storage Capacity hereunder based on the actual
capacity and capabilities of the Facility determined by such Storage Capacity Test(s).

  B.  Test Results and Re-Setting of Effective Storage Capacity. No later than five (5)
Business Days following any Storage Capacity Test, Seller shall submit a testing report detailing
results and findings of the test. The report shall include Facility meter readings and plant log
sheets verifying the operating conditions and output of the Facility. In accordance with Section
4.7 of the Agreement, Part II.I below, the Effective Storage Capacity determined pursuant to a
Storage Capacity Test (in the case of the Effective Storage Capacity, up to, but not in excess of,
  shall become the new Effective Storage Capacity at the beginning of the day following
the completion of the test for calculating the Monthly Payment and all other purposes under this
Agreement.

Storage Capacity Test Procedures

PART I.  GENERAL.

Each Storage Capacity Test (including the initial Storage Capacity Test and all re-performances
thereof) shall be conducted in accordance with Prudent Operating Practices, all operating
restrictions applicable to the Facility, and the provisions of this Exhibit L. For ease of reference,
a Storage Capacity Test is sometimes referred to in this Exhibit L as a “SCT”. Buyer or its
representative may be present for the SCT and may, for informational purposes only, use its own
metering equipment (at Buyer’s sole cost).

PART II.  REQUIREMENTS APPLICABLE TO ALL STORAGE CAPACITY TESTS.

Note: Seller shall have the right and option in its sole discretion to install storage capacity in
excess of the initial Storage Contract Capacity of  ; provided, for all purposes of this
Agreement, the amount of Effective Storage Capacity shall never be deemed to exceed  .

  A.  Purpose of Test. Each SCT shall:

  (1)  Determine an updated Effective Storage Capacity;

  B.  Test Elements. Each SCT shall include the following test elements:

  •  The measurement of discharging energy, as measured by the Facility
  Meter or other mutually agreed meter, that is discharged from the Facility

  Exhibit L - 1
   to the Delivery Point until the Stored Energy Level reaches zero MWh as
  indicated by the battery management system (“Energy Out”);

  •  Electrical output at maximum discharging capacity at the Facility Meter
  (MW);

C.  Parameters. During each SCT, the following parameters shall be measured and
  recorded simultaneously for the Facility, at ten (10) minute intervals:

  (1)  discharge time (minutes);
  (2)  discharging energy (MWh);
  (3)  discharging power (MW);
  (4)  Stored Energy Level (MWh).

D.  Site Conditions. During each SCT, the following conditions at the Site shall be
  measured and recorded simultaneously at thirty (30) minute intervals:

  (1)  Relative humidity (%);
  (2)  Barometric pressure (inches Hg) near the horizontal centerline of the
  Facility; and
  (3)  Ambient air Temperature (°F).

E.  Test Conditions.

  (i)  General. At all times during a SCT, the Facility shall be operated in
  compliance with Prudent Operating Practices and all operating protocols
  recommended, required or established by the manufacturer for operation at
  maximum charging capacity and maximum discharging capacity.
  (ii)  Abnormal Conditions. If abnormal operating conditions that prevent the
  recordation of any required parameter occur during a SCT, Seller may
  postpone or reschedule all or part of such SCT in accordance with Part II.F
  below.
  (iii)  Instrumentation and Metering. Seller shall provide all instrumentation,
  metering and data collection equipment required to perform the SCT. The
  instrumentation, metering and data collection equipment electrical meters
  shall be calibrated in accordance with Prudent Operating Practice.

F.  Incomplete Test. If any SCT is not completed in accordance herewith, Buyer may
  in its sole discretion: (i) accept the results up to the time the SCT stopped; (ii)
  require that the portion of the SCT not completed, be completed within a
  reasonable specified time period; or (iii) require that the SCT be entirely repeated.
  Notwithstanding the above, if Seller is unable to complete a SCT due to a Force
  Majeure Event or the actions or inactions of Buyer or the CAISO or the PTO or
  the Transmission Provider, Seller shall be permitted to reconduct such SCT on

  Exhibit L - 2
   dates and at times reasonably acceptable to the Parties.

G.  Final Report. Within five (5) Business Days after the completion of any SCT,
  Seller shall prepare and submit to Buyer a written report of the results of the SCT,
  which report shall include:

  (1)  a record of the personnel present during the SCT that served in an
  operating, testing, monitoring or other such participatory role;
  (2)  the measured data for each parameter set forth in Part II.A through C,
  including copies of the raw data taken during the test;
  (3)  the level of Effective Storage Capacity, Energy In, Energy Out, charging
  capacity, the current charge and discharge Ramp Rate, and Stored Energy
  Level determined by the SCT, including supporting calculations; and
  (4)  Seller’s statement of either Seller’s acceptance of the SCT or Seller’s
  rejection of the SCT results and reason(s) therefor.

  Within ten (10) Business Days after receipt of such report, Buyer shall notify
  Seller in writing of either Buyer’s acceptance of the SCT results or Buyer’s
  rejection of the SCT and reason(s) therefor.

  If either Party rejects the results of any SCT, such SCT shall be repeated in
  accordance with Part II.F.

H.  Supplementary Storage Capacity Test Protocol. No later than sixty (60) days
  prior to commencing Facility construction, Seller shall deliver to Buyer for its
  review and approval (such approval not to be unreasonably delayed or withheld)
  an updated supplement to this Exhibit L with additional and supplementary
  details, procedures and requirements applicable to Storage Capacity Tests based
  on the then current design of the Facility (“Supplementary Storage Capacity
  Test Protocol”). Thereafter, from time to time, Seller may deliver to Buyer for
  its review and approval (such approval not to be unreasonably delayed or
  withheld) any Seller recommended updates to the then current Supplementary
  Storage Capacity Test Protocol. The initial Supplementary Storage Capacity Test
  Protocol (and each update thereto), once approved by Buyer, shall be deemed an

I.  Adjustment to Effective Storage Capacity. The total amount of discharging
  energy delivered to the Delivery Point (expressed in MWh AC) during the first
  four (4) hours of discharge (up to, but not in excess of,  ), shall be divided
  by four (4) hours to determine the Effective Storage Capacity, which shall be
  expressed in MW AC, and shall be the new Effective Storage Capacity in
  accordance with Section 4.7 of the Agreement until updated pursuant to a
  subsequent Storage Capacity Test.

 Part III.  INITIAL SUPPLEMENTARY STORAGE CAPACITY TEST PROTOCOL

  The initial Supplementary Storage Capacity Test Protocol outlined below shall be
  subject to any approved terms and conditions set forth in a Supplementary Storage
  Capacity Test Protocol in accordance with Part II.H above.

  A.  Procedure:

  (1)  System Starting State: The Facility shall be balanced using OEM
  procedures as appropriate and will be in the on-line state at the Minimum
  Stored Energy Level.
  (2)  Record the initial value of the Facility State-of-Charge (“SOC”).
  (3)  Charge the Facility at the maximum charging capacity until the battery
  reaches the maximum SOC allowed at that rate. Continue charging the
  Facility at the fixed maximum battery voltage (CV charging). Stop the
  Facility charge routine when the battery has reached the desired SOC, not
  to exceed six hours of charging.
  (4)  Following an agreed-upon rest period, command a real power discharge
  that results in an AC power output of the Facility’s maximum discharging
  capacity and maintain the discharging state until the earlier of (a) the
  Facility has discharged at the maximum discharging level for four (4)
  consecutive hours, (b) the Facility has reached zero percent (0%) state of
  charge (the “Minimum Stored Energy Level”), or (c) the sustained
  discharging level is at least 2% less than the maximum discharging
  capacity.
  (5)  Record and store the AC Energy discharged (in MWh) as measured at the
  Facility Meter. Such data point shall be used for purposes of calculation of
  the Effective Storage Capacity.
  (6)  If the Facility has not reached the Minimum Stored Energy Level pursuant
  to Part III.A.4, continue discharging the Facility until it reaches the
  Minimum Stored Energy Level.
  (7)  Record and store the AC Energy discharged (in MWh) as measured at the
  Facility Metering Points. “Energy Out” means that total AC Energy
  discharged (in MWh) as measured at the Facility Metering Point
  associated with Charging Energy from the commencement of discharging
  pursuant to Part III.A.4 until the Facility has reached the Minimum Stored
  Energy Level pursuant to either Part III.A.4 or Part III.A.6, as applicable.
  All separately metered Facility Station Use shall be excluded from the
  measurement of Energy Out.
  (8)  Test Results: The resulting Effective Storage Capacity measurement is the
  sum of the total discharging energy at the Facility Meter divided by four
  (4) hours.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the City Council:

  1. Approve Agreement No. A-9686, an MOU by and between the City of Palmdale
  and WM; and,

  2. Authorize the Interim City Manager or his designee to execute Agreement No. A-
  9686, an MOU by and between the City and WM, and take actions necessary to
  implement and administer.

BACKGROUND

This MOU is brought forward pursuant to Resolution No. PC-2025-009, which approved
the fourth Modification (MOD) 24-0024 to CUP 98-12 and determined that the
Addendum prepared for the project is consistent with the previously certified
Environmental Impact Report (State Clearinghouse No. 1990010988). The project was
originally approved under MOD 24-0024 by the Planning Commission on November 13,
2025.

MOD 24-0024 authorizes the expansion and reconfiguration of the existing Antelope
Valley Recycling and Disposal Facility from 185 acres to 351 acres, expand the
operational footprint from 125 acres to 181 acres, and install an equipment pad and
equipment related to the addition of a renewable natural gas (RNG) facility.

DISCUSSION

MOU, Agreement No. A-9686, formalizes additional commitments agreed to by the
applicant in conjunction with the approved modification. The MOU is intended to be
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: MOU Agreement No. A-9686 Pursuant to CUP 98-12
February 18, 2026
Page 2

legally binding upon project approval and becomes effective upon obtaining all required
permits and approvals.

The MOU supports the City’s obligations under Senate Bill 1383, which requires the
annual procurement of 12,486 tons of recovered organic waste products and increases
the capacity to accept illegally dumped material per year within the City at no cost.

The MOU is structured in two phases, beginning with Phase 1.

Phase 1, commencing in January 2026, requires the applicant to procure recovered
organic waste products to assist the City in meeting Senate Bill 1383 requirements and
to accept up to 500 tons of illegally dumped material generated within the City annually
at no cost.

Phase 2, contingent upon securing the remaining approvals, includes a one-time
contribution of $200,000 toward roadway improvements on Tierra Subida Avenue and
an increased acceptance of 1,000 additional tons of illegally dumped materials per year
at no cost. When combined with Phase 1, the total annual acceptance would be up to
1,500 tons. These commitments are consistent with the approved project and remain
within the scope of the previously approved entitlements and environmental analysis.

$0; There is no fiscal impact associated with this action.

BACKGROUND

The City’s Five-Year Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) is updated annually to guide
planning and budgeting for major capital projects. All departments review the current CIP
and submit proposed projects for consideration. Based on changing needs and priorities,
existing projects may be revised or deferred, and new projects may be added.

Final funding decisions are made through the City Council’s adoption of the annual CIP
budget, which sets capital spending priorities for the upcoming fiscal year.

DISCUSSION

The 2025–2030 Five-Year Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) provides a planning roadmap
for capital improvements over the next five years. Projects are organized into five
categories: General/Facility, Parks and Recreation, Street Improvement,
Traffic/Transportation, and Watershed Resources. The CIP prioritizes projects based on
available funding and staff capacity, with specific projects selected annually for funding
through the budget process.

The proposed Five-Year Capital Improvement Work Plan includes 74 projects with an
estimated total cost of $416 million. A condensed project list is attached for quick

SUBJECT:  APPROVE SECOND AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT WITH
  SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA REGIONAL RAIL AUTHORITY (SCRRA)
  FOR ADDITIONAL DESIGN REVIEW SERVICES FOR THE
  PALMDALE BOULEVARD AND SIERRA HIGHWAY RAILROAD
  CROSSING SAFETY UPGRADES PROJECT, AND INCREASING
  SERVICE COSTS OF $445,500

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the City Council:

  1. Approve Second Amendment to Agreement No. A-7943 with Southern California
  Regional Rail Authority (SCRRA) for additional design review services for the
  Palmdale Boulevard and Sierra Highway Railroad Crossing Safety Upgrades
  project, and increasing the service costs of $445,500; and,

  2. Authorize the Interim City Manager or his designee to execute the Second
  Amendment to Agreement No. A-7943 with Southern California Regional Rail
  Authority (SCRRA) for minor and/or non-substantial changes.

BACKGROUND

On March 6, 2013, the City Council authorized a Memorandum of Understanding
approving $25,000,000 of Measure R Equity Grant funds for improvements to State
Route 138 (Palmdale Blvd.) between 5th Street East and 10th Street East, including at-
grade railroad safety improvements. A budget of $150,000 was allocated for FY 2013-
14 through FY 2015-16.

On May 4, 2022, Amendment No. 1 was executed for an additional $171,600 to address
increased design costs resulting from ongoing coordination among Caltrans, the
California Public Utilities Commission, Union Pacific, and the City.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Agrmt No. A-7943 Second Amendment with SCRRA
February 18, 2026
Page 2

DISCUSSION

Since the initiation of the SR 138 (Palmdale Boulevard) at-grade crossing improvement
project and the filing of the City’s Formal Application with the California Public Utilities
Commission (CPUC), the City has used existing project funds to advance design and
coordination to reach the current design milestones. These expenditures have included
consultant engineering for geometric refinements, traffic signal and preemption design,
preparation and submittal of technical exhibits (including preemption calculations), and
participation in CPUC proceedings and technical meetings with Union Pacific Railroad
(UPRR), the Rail Safety Division (RSD), Caltrans, and SCRRA.

Additional funding is now required to complete the final design, address remaining agency
comments, and implement the terms under the proposed Settlement Agreement with the
CPUC parties. The requested funds will be used to finalize Plans, Specifications, and
Estimates and to complete remaining coordination with UPRR, Caltrans, and Metrolink.

Southern California Regional Rail Authority (SCRRA), as owner-operator of one of the
railroad tracks, provides oversight, review, and independent quality assurance of the
Project Approval/Environmental Document (PA/ED) and the Plans, Specifications, and
Estimates (PS&E). SCRRA is also responsible for the ultimate approval of each of these
documents. As such, the City must reimburse SCRRA for its efforts in reviewing and
providing comments on the project documents. Amendment No. 2, if approved, would
increase the amount of reimbursable funding for SCRRA to complete the design reviews
and is necessary due to the scope-of-work revision previously approved by Council in
April 2022 and the extended project timeline.

FISCAL IMPACT

$445,500; This project is funded using Measure R Equity Grant funds. Funds are
budgeted and available in FY 2025-26.

  and public spaces with existing programming that promotes active fun for
  everyone.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the City Council:

  1. Discuss the matter and provide direction to staff.

BACKGROUND

Palmdale Municipal Code 2.08.040 states that regular meetings of the City Council “will
be held on the first and third Tuesday of each.”

Specifically, PMC 2.08.040 states in full:

  2.08.040 Regular meeting day, time and place.

  Regular meetings of the City Council will be held on the first and third
  Tuesday of each month. Meetings of the City Council shall be held at
  38300 Sierra Highway, Suite B, Palmdale, California. The regular
  meeting will begin at 5:00 p.m., followed by the closed session meeting.
  If all matters on the agenda for any regular meeting have not been
  considered by the City Council by the hour of 10:30 p.m., or such earlier
  or later time as may be fixed by a majority vote of the City Council, then
  the regular meeting may be adjourned to the next succeeding Tuesday,
  at the same time and the exact location, unless a different day, time or
  location is specified in the order of adjournment. When so adjourned,
  each adjourned meeting shall be a regular meeting for all purposes. At
  least twice a year, the City Council shall meet to receive and/or present
